IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p187/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p187/r3.speaker: بعض المتقدمين
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p187/r3.claim: Some early reciters read the truncated vocative يا مالك in the people’s call to the keeper of Hell.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p187/r3.anchor: وقرأ بعض المتقدمين: ونادوا يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك

DAMGHANI:v1p383/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r7.claim: Qaḍā can mean bringing death, as Pharaoh’s people ask for death and Moses’ blow kills a man.
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r7.anchor: الخامس : قضى نزل الموت قوله تعالى

DAMGHANI:v1p450/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p450/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p450/r6.claim: Nidāʾ can mean calling for help; the people of the Fire’s appeal for water is another example.
DAMGHANI:v1p450/r6.anchor: النداء الاستغاثة قوله تعالى في سورة الزخرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p466#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p466#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p466#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari adduces their pleas to be removed from Hell or for death as examples of confused speech despite knowing the outcome.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p466#2/r6.anchor: ألا تراهم يقولون ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r2.claim: The closing passage first depicts the fate of those who accept the true call and then the fate of those who deny it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r2.anchor: the fate of those people is mentioned who will profess faith in this true call; then the fate of those people is depicted

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r4.claim: The disbelievers' silence and their later call to Mālik do not conflict: these are states occurring over long stretches of time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r4.anchor: تقدم أنهم مبلسون، أي ساكتون، وهذه أحوال لهم في أزمان متطاولة، فلا تعارض بين سكوتهم وندائهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r5.claim: The majority read “O Mālik” with the full name; several readers shorten it to “O Māl” using the dialect that anticipates the omitted letter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يا مالك. وقرأ عبد الله، وعلى، وابن وثاب، والأعمش: يا مال، بالترخيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r6.speaker: أبو السرار الغنوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r6.claim: Abū al-Sarrār al-Ghanawī reads yā Māl with a final ḍamma, treating it as an independent name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو السرار الغنوي: يا مال، بالبناء على الضم، جعل اسما على حياله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r7.claim: The lām in “so that he may end us” expresses a request or wish: they ask to die once so the punishment will not recur.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r7.anchor: واللام في: ليقض لام الطلب والرغبة. والمعنى: يمتنا مرة حتى لا يتكرر عذابنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r8.claim: Mālik answers that they will remain in Hell and never leave it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r8.anchor: قال: أي ما لك، إنكم ماكثون: أي مقيمون في النار لا تبرحون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Mālik answers after one thousand years; other reports give one hundred, eighty, or forty years.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يجيبهم بعد مضي ألف سنة، وقال نوف: بعد مائة، وقيل: ثمانين

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r18.claim: An extended contrast of believers’ and disbelievers’ fates in the Hereafter follows these examples.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r18.anchor: there is an extended contrast of the fate of believers and disbelievers in the Hereafter (vv. 66–78)

NAHHAS:v4p120/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p120/r11.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v4p120/r11.claim: Mujahid says they did not understand yā Mālik until they heard Abdullah's reading yā Māl.
NAHHAS:v4p120/r11.anchor: قال مجاهد ما كنا ندري معنى يا مالك حتى سمعنا في قراءة عبد الله

NAHHAS:v4p120/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p120/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p120/r12.claim: Yā Māl is apocope of Mālik, a shortening Arabs often use for Mālik and ʿĀmir, though this reading differs from the muṣḥaf.
NAHHAS:v4p120/r12.anchor: هذا على الترخيم والعرب ترخم مالكا وعامرا كثيرا إلا أن هذا مخالف للسواد

NAHHAS:v4p120/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p120/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p120/r13.claim: The shortened vocative yā Māl is the more eloquent of two Arabic forms; a cited line shortens Ḥārith to Ḥār, while another dialect treats the remainder as the name unchanged.
NAHHAS:v4p120/r13.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول يا مال أقبل فيجعلون ما بقي اسما على حاله

SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r1.claim: The common reading retains مالك without truncation.
SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r1.anchor: العامة من غير ترخيم. وعلي بن أبي طالب

SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وعبد الله وابن وثاب والأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r2.claim: These readers use truncated يا مال according to the dialect that anticipates the omitted ending.
SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r2.anchor: وعلي بن أبي طالب وعبد الله وابن وثاب والأعمش " يا مال " مرخما على لغة من ينتظر.

SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r3.speaker: أبو السوار الغنوي
SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r3.claim: Abū al-Sawwār al-Ghanawī reads يا مال with ḍamma, according to the dialect that does not anticipate the ending.
SAMIN-DURR:43:77/r3.anchor: وأبو السوار الغنوي " يا مال " مبنيا على الضم على لغة من لا ينوي.

ZAJJAJ:v4p419#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p419#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p419#2/r5.claim: A reported variant shortens يا مالك to يا مال and gives the lām kasra; grammarians call this truncation, common in poetry, but Zajjāj dislikes it because it conflicts with the codex.
ZAJJAJ:v4p419#2/r5.anchor: وقد رويت يا مال - بغير كاف، وبكسر اللام -

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p206/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p206/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p206/r7.claim: The closing section first tells believers and disbelievers their respective fates, then assures the Prophet to disregard mockers, and ends by restating tawḥīd and rejecting intercession as a means of rescue.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p206/r7.anchor: first the believers are informed of their good fate and the disbelievers are informed of their evil fate

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p212/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p212/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p212/r2.claim: The people address Mālik, the jailer of Hell, asking him to request that God end their lives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p212/r2.anchor: They will ask the jailer of Hell: O Master! If there is no possibility of any mercy on us please request your Lord to finish us.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p212/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p212/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p212/r3.claim: Mālik answers that they cannot be destroyed and must remain in Hell; death, their last support in despair, is withheld from them as the greatest deprivation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p212/r3.anchor: The last support to despair is death, but these people will be deprived of even this support, and this indeed is their greatest deprivation.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Mālik leaves them for a thousand years before replying that they will remain.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ ونادوا يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك ﴾ قال مكث عنهم ألف سنة ثم قال إنكم ماكثون

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r2.claim: Sufyān reports that Ibn Masʿūd's reading has the vocative يا مال instead of يا مالك.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r2.anchor: قال سفيان الثوري وفي حرف ابن مسعود ونادوا يا مال ليقض علينا ربك

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r3.claim: Yaʿlā ibn Umayya reports hearing the Prophet recite the verse on the pulpit.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#2/r3.anchor: عن صفوان بن يعلى بن أمية عن أبيه قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو على المنبر يقرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r1.speaker: بعض الآثار
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r1.claim: An unspecified report says hunger is imposed on the people of Hell until it equals their other torment, so they call Malik. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r1.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار يلقى على أهل النار الجوع حتى يعدل ما هم فيه من العذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r2.claim: They ask Malik to request that his Lord kill them and grant relief; saying ‘your Lord’ is an appeal for help, not rejection.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r2.anchor: أي ليمتنا من قضى عليه إذا أماته ومرادهم سل ربك

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r3.claim: Their call can coexist with despair as they fall silent at times and cry out at others during prolonged punishment; one objection is that alternating states do not suit the continuous clause ‘they are despairing.’
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r3.anchor: لأنه صراخ وتمني للموت من فرط الشدة وأما على التفسير الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r4.claim: Another reply says the coordinating wāw does not require sequence, so calling need not follow despair; Alusi notes the circumstantial clause remains tied to their abiding state.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r4.anchor: وقيل إن نادوا معطوف بالواو وهي لا تقتضي ترتيبا ولا يخفى أن تلك الجملة حالية

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r5.speaker: علي وابن مسعود وابن وثاب والأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r5.claim: Ali, Ibn Masud, Ibn Waththab, and al-Aʿmash read ‘yā Māl,’ using the language that anticipates the omitted ending.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن مسعود وابن وثاب والأعمش يا مال بالترخيم على لغة من ينتظر

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r6.speaker: أبو السوار
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r6.claim: Abu al-Sawwar reads the shortened name according to the language that does not anticipate the omitted ending.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو السوار يا مال بالترخيم أيضا لكن على لغة من لم ينتظر

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r7.speaker: ابن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r7.claim: Ibn Jinni says truncation signals collapsed strength and humbled souls, rather than deliberate stylistic flourish.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r7.anchor: وللترخيم في هذاالموضع سر وذلك أنهم لعظم ما همفيه ضعفت قواهم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas objects that the people of Hell would be too occupied for the unusual shortened form; the reply is that helplessness and constriction force the truncation.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r8.anchor: ما أشغل أهل النار على الترخيم مشيرا بذلك إلى إنكارها فإن ما للتعجيب

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r9.claim: The poetic shortened vocative is explained by inability and lack of room to finish the word, not intentional verbal artistry.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r9.anchor: والحق يا مال غير ما تصف بل للعجز وضيق المجال عن الإتمام

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r10.claim: Malik says they remain forever with no escape through death or otherwise; this deepens despair, and their hopelessness does not prevent the answer from tormenting them.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r10.anchor: مقيمون في العذاب أبدا لا خلاص لكم منه بموت ولا غيره وهذا تقنيط ونكاية لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r11.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r11.claim: Some hear mockery in ‘remaining,’ since the word can suggest a stay that ends and involves waiting; the delayed answer may heighten it.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r11.anchor: وذكر بعض الأجلة أن فيه استهزاء لأنه أقام المكث مقام الخلود والمكث يشعر بالانقطاع

ALUSI-FULL:v25p103/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p103/r1.speaker: ابنعباس
ALUSI-FULL:v25p103/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Malik answers them after a thousand years have passed.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p103/r1.anchor: قال ابنعباس يجيبهم بعد مضي ألف سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v25p103/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p103/r2.speaker: نوف
ALUSI-FULL:v25p103/r2.claim: Nauf says the answer comes after one hundred years.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p103/r2.anchor: وقال نوف : بعد مائة وقيل ثمانين وقيل أربعين

ALUSI-FULL:v25p103/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p103/r3.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v25p103/r3.claim: Other reports estimate that Malik answers after eighty or forty years.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r4.claim: Malik is the keeper of Hell, whom its inhabitants call upon.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r5.claim: They ask God to end their lives so they can rest; al-Baghawi says Malik answers after a thousand years that they will remain in torment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r5.anchor: {ليقض علينا ربك} ليمتنا ربك فنستريح فيجيبهم مالك بعد ألف سنة، {قال إنكم ماكثون}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r6.claim: The Prophet reports that Hell's people call Malik unanswered for forty years, then ask God to release them; after silence lasting twice the world's span, they are told to be silent and utter only donkey-like gasps.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال [النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم] (2) : "إن أهل النار يدعون مالكا فلا يجيبهم أربعين عاما

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r1.claim: A reading addresses him as يا مال, shortened by truncation and with either kasra or damma.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r1.anchor: وقرىء «يا مال» على الترخيم مكسورا ومضموما

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r2.claim: Their shortened address may signal weakness; asking God to end them is a cry and wish for death from torment, not inconsistent with despair.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r2.anchor: ولعله إشعار بأنهم لضعفهم لا يستطيعون تأدية اللفظ بالتمام

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r3.claim: They ask their Lord to cause them to die; this is a cry and wish for death from extreme severity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r3.anchor: والمعنى سل ربنا أن يقضي علينا من قضى عليه إذا أماته

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r4.claim: They have no escape through death or any other means.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:77-79/r4.anchor: لا خلاص لكم بموت ولا بغيره

DURR-FULL:v7p394/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r3.speaker: يعلى بن أمية
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r3.claim: Yaʿlā reports hearing the Prophet recite the address to Mālik from the pulpit.
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r3.anchor: عن يعلى بن أمية قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ على المنبر {ونادوا يا مالك}

DURR-FULL:v7p394/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r4.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r4.claim: ʿAlī reports hearing the Prophet recite the address to Mālik from the pulpit.
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r4.anchor: عن علي أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ على المنبر {ونادوا يا مالك}

DURR-FULL:v7p394/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading likewise has يا مالك.
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود {ونادوا يا مالك}

DURR-FULL:v7p394/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r6.speaker: يعلى بن أمية
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r6.claim: Yaʿlā reports the Prophet's full reading of the damned asking Mālik that their Lord finish them.
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r6.anchor: عن يعلى بن أمية قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ على المنبر {ونادوا يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك}

DURR-FULL:v7p394/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Mālik waits a thousand years before answering that the damned will remain.
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ونادوا يا مالك} قال: مكث عنهم ألف سنة ثم يجيبهم {إنكم ماكثون}

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3286#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3286#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3286#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says a thousand years passed before the inhabitants of Hell called to Malik, who then answered that they would remain.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3286#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ونادوا يا مالك قال : مكث عنهم الف سنة ، ثم يجيبهم : انهم ماكثون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r1.claim: Their call is either circumstantial from their despair or coordinated with that clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r1.anchor: جملة { ونادوا } حال من ضمير { وهم فيه مبلسون } ( الزخرف : 75 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r2.claim: If circumstantial, their despair follows the call and Malik’s answer; if coordinated, past tense presents a future event as already certain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r2.anchor: وحكي نداؤهم بصيغة الماضي مع أنه مما سيقع يوم القيامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r3.claim: Malik is the angel appointed over Hell, whom its inhabitants address to convey their appeal to God as an intercessor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r3.anchor: و ( مالك ) المنادى اسم الملك الموكل بجهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r4.claim: The lām is an imperative used as supplication; an absent addressee is addressed for conveyance, or a present one is treated as absent to show reverence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r4.anchor: واللام في { ليقض علينا ربك } لام الأمر بمعنى الدعاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r5.claim: Qaḍā means to kill or end life, as in the account of Moses striking a man and ending his life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r5.anchor: والقضاء بمعنى : الإماتة كقوله : { فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r6.claim: They ask God to end their lives to escape awareness of torment; the answer that they will remain rules out both death and exit, ending any further plea.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r6.anchor: سألوا الله أن يزيل عنهم الحياة ليستريحوا من إحساس العذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud reportedly recited yā Māl with the kāf omitted by tarḫīm; Ibn ʿAbbas replied that Hell’s inhabitants had more pressing concerns than shortening the name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r7.anchor: ما روي أن ابن مسعود قرأ ( ونادوا يا مال ) بحذف الكاف على الترخيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r8.speaker: ابن جني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r8.claim: Al-Kashshaf’s explanation, identified by Ibn al-Jinnī through al-Tībī, is that their weakness and humiliation shorten their speech, making truncation apt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r8.anchor: وأراد ببعضهم ابن جني فيما ذكره الطيبي أن ابن جني قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r9.speaker: يعلى بن أمية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r9.claim: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Yaʿla ibn Umayya says he heard the Prophet recite yā Mālik with the kāf on the pulpit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r9.anchor: وفي ( صحيح البخاري ) عن يعلى بن أمية سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ على المنبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya cites Abu al-Dardaʾ’s report of the shortened form from the Prophet and infers that the Prophet recited both forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطية : وقراءة ( ونادوا يا مال ) رواها أبو الدرداء عن النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r11.claim: Only the form with kāf is mutawātir; the shortened form is transmitted singly and therefore is not Qur’an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p259/r11.anchor: وتواترت قراءة إثبات الكاف وبقيت الأخرى مروية بالآحاد فلم تكن قرآنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r7.claim: Malik is the keeper of the Fire whom its inhabitants call upon.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r7.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى عن أهل النار أنهم ينادون مالكا خازن النار،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r8.claim: The imperative form expresses a plea that the Lord put an end to them by making them die.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r8.anchor: فيقولون على معنى الرغبة التي هي في صيغة الأمر ليقض علينا ربك أي ليمتنا مرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r9.claim: The Prophet recited يا مالك with kaf, the majority reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r9.anchor: وقرأ النبي عليه السلام على المنبر: «يا مالك» بالكاف، وهي قراءة الجمهور.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود ويحيى والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r10.claim: Ibn Masud, Yahya, and al-A'mash read shortened يا مال; it is also related from Ali and the Prophet through Abu al-Darda.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود ويحيى والأعمش: «يا مال» بالترخيم، ورويت عن علي بن أبي طالب،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r11.claim: Here قضى means death, as when Moses struck a man and killed him in 28:15.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r11.anchor: والقضاء في هذه الآية بمعنى الموت، كما قال تعالى: فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه [القصص: 15]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says Malik waits one thousand years after their plea before answering that they will remain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r12.anchor: أن مالكا يقيم بعد سؤالهم ألف سنة، وقال نوف: مائة سنة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r13.speaker: نوف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r13.claim: Nawf says Malik waits one hundred years before answering.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r13.anchor: ألف سنة، وقال نوف: مائة سنة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r14.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r14.claim: Another report gives an eighty-year wait.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r14.anchor: وقال نوف: مائة سنة، وقيل: ثمانين سنة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r15.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r15.claim: Abd Allah ibn Umar gives a forty-year wait before Malik answers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r15.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمر: وأربعين سنة، ثم حينئذ يقول لهم: إنكم ماكثون.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن مسعود وابن يعمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r1.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Masud, and Ibn Ya'mar read yā māl with the kāf omitted and kasra on the lām.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r1.anchor: وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب رضى الله عنه وابن مسعود وابن يعمر يا مال بغير كاف مع كسر اللام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls the form truncation (tarḫim), but dislikes it because it differs from the written muṣḥaf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج وهذا يسميه النحويون الترخيم ولكني أكرهها لمخالفة المصحف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r3.claim: Exegetes identify Malik as the keeper of Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون يدعون مالكا خازن النار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r4.claim: The plea means “let Him put us to death.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r4.anchor: أي ليمتنا والمعنى أهم توسلوا به ليسأل اله تعالى لهم الموت فيستريحوا من العذاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r5.claim: They appeal to Malik to ask God for death so they can rest from the torment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r5.anchor: والمعنى أهم توسلوا به ليسأل اله تعالى لهم الموت فيستريحوا من العذاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r6.claim: One report says Malik delayed his answer for forty years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r6.anchor: أربعون عاما قاله عبد الله بن عمرو ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r7.speaker: أنس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r7.claim: Anas says Malik delayed his answer for thirty years.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says Malik delayed his answer for a thousand years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r8.anchor: الثالث ألف سنة قاهل ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r9.speaker: كعب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r9.claim: Ka'b says Malik delayed his answer for a hundred years.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r10.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r10.claim: Muqatil says Malik remained silent until God revealed that he should answer them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r10.anchor: أنه سكت حتى أوحى الله إليه أن أجبهم قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r11.claim: Another view says the gap between their call and the answer increased their disgrace and humiliation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r11.anchor: والثاني لأن بعد ما بين النداء والجواب أخزى لهم وأذل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r12.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r12.claim: Al-Mawardi says Malik replied that they would remain in the punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#5/r12.anchor: قال الماوردي فرد عليهم مالك فقال ﴿ إنكم ماكثون ﴾ أي مقيمون في العذاب

BURSEVI:v8p303/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p303/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p303/r1.claim: The condemned ask Malik to ask his Lord to end their lives so they can rest; qada ʿalayhi is an idiom for killing.
BURSEVI:v8p303/r1.anchor: {ليقض علينا ربك} ؛ أي : ليمتنا حتى نستريح من قضى عليه إذا أماته.

BURSEVI:v8p303/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p303/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p303/r2.claim: Their cry for death does not conflict with their despair: it is a wail and wish for death caused by extreme torment.
BURSEVI:v8p303/r2.anchor: وهذا لا ينافي ما ذكر من إبلاسهم ؛ لأنه جؤار ؛ أي : صياح وتمن للموت لفرط الشدة.

BURSEVI:v8p303/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p303/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p303/r3.claim: Malik's answer is delayed: they may call for forty years, a hundred, or a thousand; al-Tibyan gives forty days, and delay deepens grief.
BURSEVI:v8p303/r3.anchor: مالك مجيبا بعد أربعين سنة ، يعني : ينادون ملكا أربعين سنة

BURSEVI:v8p303#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p303#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p303#2/r1.claim: Makith means staying while awaiting; they remain forever in torment with no escape by death or otherwise, and wail like a donkey.
BURSEVI:v8p303#2/r1.anchor: المكث : ثبات مع انتظار ؛ أي : مقيمون في العذاب أبدا لا خلاص لكم منه بموت

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r1.claim: The people of the Fire call its keepers after tasting its punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r1.anchor: هذا نداء أهل النار لخزانها حين ذاقوا عذابها

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r2.claim: They ask God to kill them so they can rest from the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r2.anchor: أي يميتنا ، طلبوا الموت ليستريحوا به من عذاب النار

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r3.claim: Mālik says they will remain alive in its punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r3.anchor: أي لابثون في عذابها أحياء , وفي مدة ما بين ندائهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr gives forty years between their call and Mālik’s answer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r4.anchor: أربعون سنة ، قاله عبد الله بن عمرو

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives one thousand years; al-Māwardī says the delay increases their humiliation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p239/r7.anchor: ألف سنة , قاله ابن عباس , لأن بعد ما بين النداء والجواب

MUQATIL:43:74-78/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r5.claim: Malik is the keeper of Hell.
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r5.anchor: وهو خازن جهنم، فقال: ماذا تريدون؟

MUQATIL:43:74-78/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r6.claim: The people of Hell ask Malik to have their Lord put an end to them; Malik stays silent forty years until God orders a reply that they will remain in punishment.
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r6.anchor: فيسكت عنهم مالك، فلا يجيبهم مقدار أربعين سنة، ثم يوحي الله تعالى إلى مالك بعد أربعين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r1.claim: When they despair of any respite in punishment, they call Mālik, the keeper of Hell.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r1.anchor: لما ايسوا من فتور العذاب نادوا يا مالك وهو خازن النار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads yā Māl, with the name shortened by tarḫīm; Ibn ʿAbbās quips that Hell's occupants have more pressing concerns than shortening names.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r2.anchor: وقيل لابن عباس ان ابن مسعود قرأ يا مال فقال ما أشغل أهل النار عن الترخيم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r3.claim: They ask Mālik to request their death; qada ʿalayhi means killed him, as in the account of Moses striking a man and killing him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r3.anchor: ليمتنا من قضى عليه اذا اماته فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه والمعنى سل ربك أن يقضى علينا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r4.claim: They will remain in the punishment and cannot escape it by death or respite.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#5/r4.anchor: في العذاب لا تتخلصون عنه بموت ولا فتور

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r1.claim: Malik is the keeper of Hell, created for wrath; when he rebukes the Fire with a roar, it devours itself.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r1.anchor: وهو خازن جهنم، خلقه لغضبه إذا زجر النار زجرة أكل بعضها بعضا

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r2.speaker: علي وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r2.claim: Ali and Ibn Masud read يا مال, omitting the kaf, contrary to the codex reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r2.anchor: وقرأ علي وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما «ونادوا يا مال» وذلك خلاف المصحف

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda and Ibn Masud report that the Prophet read يا مال, using a vocative abbreviation that deletes the end of the name.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r3.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء وابن مسعود: قرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ونادوا يا مال» باللام خاصة يعني رخم الاسم وحذف الكاف

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r4.claim: In vocative truncation, the remaining name may retain its original case or be built on damma, as though the omitted letters did not matter.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r4.anchor: ولك في آخر الاسم المرخم وجهان: أحدهما أن تبقيه على ما كان عليه قبل الحذف. والآخر أن تبنيه على الضم

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r5.claim: Mujahid says they learned that زخرف meant a house of gold, and that Abdullah's codex resolved whether the reading was Malik or Malak by giving يا مال.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: كنا لا ندري ما الزخرف حتى وجدناه في قراءة عبد الله «بيت من ذهب»

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r6.speaker: أبو بكر الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r6.claim: Al-Anbari rejects the Mujahid report as a disconnected report unsuitable as a prophetic narration, insisting scripture must be guarded against falsehood.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r6.anchor: قال أبو بكر: لا يعمل على هذا الحديث لأنه مقطوع لا يقبل مثله في الرواية عن الرسول عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r7.claim: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ya'la reports that he heard the Prophet recite the form with kaf, يامالك, from the pulpit.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r7.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري عن صفوان بن يعلى عن أبيه قال سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ على المنبر

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi prefaces a report that Hell's inmates called out to its keepers for help.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77/r8.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: بلغني أو ذكر لي أن أهل النار استغاثوا بالخزنة

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r1.claim: In al-Qurazi's report, Hell's inmates first beg its keepers to lessen the torment for one day, citing 40:49–50; when refused, they call Malik from his place in the middle of Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r1.anchor: فسألوا يوما واحدا يخفف عنهم فيه العذاب فردت عليهم: أولم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r2.claim: In al-Qurazi's report, Malik remains silent for eighty years before replying; a year is defined as 360 days, a month as thirty days, and a day as a thousand years by human reckoning.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r2.anchor: قال: فسكت عنهم لا يجيبهم ثمانين سنة، قال: والسنة ستون وثلثمائة يوم، والشهر ثلاثون يوما

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r3.claim: Al-Qurazi's report says Malik finally tells the inmates they will remain, after which Ibn al-Mubarak transmits the account.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r3.anchor: ثم لحظ إليهم بعد الثمانين فقال: «إنكم ماكثون» وذكر الحديث ذكره ابن المبارك

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r4.claim: An Abu al-Darda report from the Prophet says the inmates ask Malik to end their lives and he answers that they will remain; al-Tirmidhi transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r4.anchor: وفي حديث أبي الدرداء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r5.speaker: الأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r5.claim: Al-A'mash was told that a thousand years passed between their call and Malik's answer; al-Tirmidhi transmits the report.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r5.anchor: قال الأعمش: نبئت أن بين دعائهم وبين إجابة مالك إياهم ألف عام خرجه الترمذي

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Malik does not answer them for a thousand years, then says they will remain.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يقولون ذلك فلا يجيبهم ألف سنة، ثم يقول إنكم ماكثون

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد ونوف البكالي
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r7.claim: Mujahid and Nawf al-Bikali say a hundred years pass between the call and the answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد ونوف البكالي: بين ندائهم وإجابته إياهم مائة سنة

QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r8.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr gives the interval as forty years; Ibn al-Mubarak transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:77#2/r8.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو: أربعون سنة ذكره ابن المبارك

QASHANI:43:77/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:43:77/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:43:77/r2.claim: The keeper of Hell is called Malik because he serves those who owned the world and preferred it.
QASHANI:43:77/r2.anchor: سمي خازن النار مالكا لاختصاصه بمن ملك الدنيا وآثرها

QASHANI:43:77/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:43:77/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:43:77/r3.claim: The keeper of the garden is called Ridwan because he is associated with those with whom God is pleased and who are pleased with Him.
QASHANI:43:77/r3.anchor: كما سمى خازن الجنة رضوانا لاختصاصه بمن رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه

QASHANI:43:77/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:43:77/r4.speaker: قيل
QASHANI:43:77/r4.claim: An alternative says contentment with God's decree is the greatest gate to Him and identifies Malik with bodily nature, dark matter, or the universal animal soul governing bodies.
QASHANI:43:77/r4.anchor: وقيل: الرضا بالقضاء باب الله الأعظم وهو الطبيعة الجسمانية الموكلة بأجساد العالم

QASHANI:43:77/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:43:77/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:43:77/r5.claim: The fire is a garden for its keeper, who shares its substance, but torment for the people of Hell because their essences differ from and conflict with it.
QASHANI:43:77/r5.anchor: وإنما لا يتعذب بالنار لكونه من جوهر تلك النار فهي له جنة

QASHANI:43:77/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:43:77/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:43:77/r6.claim: They call Malik rather than God because they are wholly veiled from and distant from God, and their intentions and wishes were devoted to Malik.
QASHANI:43:77/r6.anchor: واختصاص ندائهم بمالك دون الله تعالى لاحتجابهم وبعدهم عن الله بالكلية

QASHANI:43:77/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:43:77/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:43:77/r7.claim: Their plea for death means wishing either to lose every remaining capacity and innate disposition so painful forms cease, or to lose sensation because bodily punishment is intense.
QASHANI:43:77/r7.anchor: إشارة إلى تمني زوال بقية الاستعداد بالكلية وإماتة الغريزة الفطرية

QASHANI:43:77/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:43:77/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:43:77/r8.claim: Their duration depends on rooted dispositions and accumulated sins if capacity and sound belief remain, or is eternal otherwise.
QASHANI:43:77/r8.anchor: إن كانت الاستعدادات باقية والاعتقادات صحيحة أو الخلود فيها إن لم تكن

QASHANI:43:77/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:43:77/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:43:77/r9.claim: Duration is broader than eternity, and sinner broader than primordial wretch; accordingly 43:74 may describe a long stay figuratively or everlasting punishment if it refers only to the eternally rejected.
QASHANI:43:77/r9.anchor: وكذا المجرم أعم من الشقي الأصلي وغيره

STUDYQURAN:43:77/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r1.claim: The inhabitants of Hell address Mālik, said to be Hell’s keeper.
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r1.anchor: The denizens of Hell will call to the angel Mālik, who is said to be the keeper of Hell

STUDYQURAN:43:77/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r2.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r2.claim: They ask to be destroyed so they can gain respite from the Fire’s torments.
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r2.anchor: to destroy them, so that they will receive some respite from the torments of the Fire (IK)

STUDYQURAN:43:77/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r3.claim: Their wish for destruction recalls the disbeliever’s wish on Judgment Day to be dust.
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r3.anchor: Similarly, on the Day of Judgment, the disbeliever says, “Oh, would that I were dust!” (78:40)

STUDYQURAN:43:77/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r4.claim: The request also recalls those cast in a narrow place who call to be destroyed.
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r4.anchor: when they are cast bound together into a narrow place thereof, they will, there and then, call to be destroyed (25:13)

STUDYQURAN:43:77/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r5.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r5.claim: The reply echoes that they cannot die or have punishment lightened, and that this is requital for disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r5.anchor: They will not be done away with so as to die; nor will aught of its punishment be lightened for them

STUDYQURAN:43:77/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r6.speaker: JJ, Q
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r6.claim: Mālik’s response is said to take a thousand years; he tells them they will remain there forever.
STUDYQURAN:43:77/r6.anchor: Mālik’s response, which is said to take a thousand years (JJ, Q), will be that they are to remain there everlastingly

QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r6.claim: Had they addressed Malik, their words might have been nearer to an answer, but estrangement kept them from it; they are told they remain because they rejected counsel and hated truth.
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r6.anchor: لو قالوا : ( يا ملك ) لعل أقوالهم كانت أقرب إلى الإجابة

QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r7.claim: They are told they will remain because they were counseled but refused advice and hated the truth.
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r7.anchor: نصحتم فلم تنتصحوا ، ولم تقبلوا القول في حينه

TABATABAI:43:71-77/r18.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:71-77/r18.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:71-77/r18.claim: Mālik is the king and keeper of the Fire, as reports through Sunni and Shia routes state.
TABATABAI:43:71-77/r18.anchor: مالك هو الملك الخازن للنار على ما وردت به الأخبار من طرق العامة والخاصة

TABATABAI:43:77-78/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r1.claim: They ask Mālik to petition God because they are screened from God and cannot speak to Him.
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r1.anchor: فالمعنى أنهم يسألون مالكا أن يسأل الله أن يقضي عليهم

TABATABAI:43:77-78/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r2.claim: They request death and annihilation to escape misery and painful punishment.
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r2.anchor: ويريدون بالموت الانعدام والبطلان لينجوا بذلك عما هم فيه من الشقوة وأليم العذاب

TABATABAI:43:77-78/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r3.claim: Their plea reflects their worldly belief that death is annihilation, not transition; they have already died and witnessed its reality.
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r3.anchor: فإنهم كانوا يرون في الدنيا أن الموت انعدام وفوت لا انتقال من دار إلى دار

TABATABAI:43:77-78/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r4.claim: Mālik replies that they remain in wretched life and painful punishment.
TABATABAI:43:77-78/r4.anchor: أي فيما أنتم فيه من الحياة الشقية والعذاب الأليم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Malik as the keeper of Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد خازن جهنم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the damned ask Malik to have God end their lives; Malik remains silent for forty years.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r3.claim: Muqatil explains the plea as asking God to bring death so they can rest from the torment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: لينزل علينا ربك الموت، والمعنى أنهم توسلوا بمالك إلى الله تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Malik does not answer them for a thousand years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r4.anchor: وألف سنة فيما روي عن ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r5.speaker: القرظي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r5.claim: Al-Qurazi says Malik stays silent for eighty years, each day equal to a thousand years by their reckoning, then tells them they will remain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r5.anchor: قال القرظي: لا يجيبهم ثمانين سنة، كل يوم منها كألف سنة مما تعدون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r6.claim: Muqatil glosses the answer as meaning that they remain in the torment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p77#2/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل: يقول مقيمون في العذاب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:77/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:77/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:77/r1.claim: The damned call Malik to ask that his Lord put them to death so they can rest.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:77/r1.anchor: ونادوا يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك } ليمتنا فنستريح { قال إنكم ماكثون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:77/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:77/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:77/r2.claim: Malik answers that they will remain in the torment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:77/r2.anchor: قال إنكم ماكثون } مقيمون في العذاب

ELMALILI:43:68-89/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r14.claim: Mālik is the name of the keeper of Hell.

ELMALILI:43:68-89/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r15.claim: The condemned beg God to finish their case by killing them so that they might escape the torment.

ELMALILI:43:68-89/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r16.claim: Mālik replies that they will stay: neither death nor anything else will release them.

ELMALILI:43:68-89/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r17.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Mālik’s reply comes after a thousand years; the author treats this duration as a figure for a very long time.
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r17.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan mervîdir ki bu cevap da bin sene sonra verilir

ELMALILI:43:68-89/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r18.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r18.claim: Another report gives one hundred years before the reply; the author treats the duration figures as hyperbole for a great span.

ELMALILI:43:68-89/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r19.speaker: İbn Amr
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAmr reports forty years before the reply; the author regards all three durations as figurative of great number.
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r19.anchor: İbn Amr[^11] Hazretleri’nden de kırk sene[^12] diye rivayet olunmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r4.claim: Ghafir 40:49 describes the damned asking angels to intercede for lighter punishment and being refused; here the hopeless appeal to Malik, the chief attendant, is a last request to be annihilated.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r4.anchor: Gāfir sûresinde (40/49) cehennemliklerin, burada görevli meleklerden, “azaplarının hafifletilmesi için Allah’a aracı olup dua etmelerini istedikleri”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r5.claim: Malik's answer matches the prophets' warning in the world: Hell's punishment is eternal for those who associate partners with God and deny Him and the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r5.anchor: “Cehennem azabı, Allah’a ortak koşanlar, O’nu ve âhireti inkâr edenler için ebedîdir.”

BURHAN:v2p86/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p86/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p86/r1.claim: Zarkashi argues that early hearers did not take ‘hand’ as a bodily limb: neither believers nor disbelievers objected, suggesting the figurative usage had become familiar; the sense is near power but more specific and honorific.
BURHAN:v2p86/r1.anchor: ولما لم ينقل ذلك عن مؤمن ولا كافر علم أن الأمر عندهم كان جليا لا خفاء به لأنها صفة سميت الجارحة بها مجازا

ITQAN:v3p162#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p162#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v3p162#2/r3.claim: Some read the vocative with apocope as yā Māl; a Salaf scholar objected that the people of Hell need no apocopation, while others said their distress left them unable to finish the word.
ITQAN:v3p162#2/r3.anchor: ومنه قراءة بعضهم / ونادوا يا مال / بالترخيم ولما سمعها بعض السلف قال ما أغنى أهل النار عن الترخيم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p506#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p506#2/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p506#2/r7.claim: Qaḍāʾ can mean putting someone to death.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p506#2/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن القضاء في القرآن على خمسة عشر وجها :

BURHAN:v3p116/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p116/r11.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v3p116/r11.claim: Some recite يا مال by the form of tarḫīm that awaits completion; a salaf objected to such abbreviation in Hell, while others said its inhabitants were too distressed to finish the word.
BURHAN:v3p116/r11.anchor: ولما سمعها بعض السلف قال ما أشغل أهل النار عن الترخيم

BURHAN:v4p350/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p350/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p350/r1.claim: The lām of command can express self-instruction, supplication, threat, or a declarative meaning; examples include let us carry your sins, let your Lord finish us, and whoever wills may believe.
BURHAN:v4p350/r1.anchor: ومنها امر المكلف نفسه كقوله تعالى
